And if you can refer with the pointer, you have to refer to the sketch which is under the overhead projector. You can't point to the scene, because otherwise we won't be able to see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Bos, I'm sorry to interrupt you. But this witness gave very crucial evidence in a very, very fast manner. And perhaps to help the Trial Chamber, you could go back and take it line by line. For instance, it's not clear when he was in the basement whether he was alone for a short period, whether he ever joined anybody else, whether they got joint instructions, single instructions. It's just a little bit rushed. And it's not your fault, and it's not the witness's fault, because obviously it's stressful, but if you could just stop every now and again and go over it. And I'm sorry, Witness, that I'm asking you to repeat what must be very stressful for you. But it's important evidence, and I'm afraid that we might not get the full picture if we don't hear it more slowly. I'm sorry to ask you to go over some of it a little more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, you've heard what the Judge said. So let's go back a Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts – Pages 6091 to 6104. little in time and let me try to clarify some of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Specifically, Mr. Bos, the instructions in the basement, and then the appearance of somebody with a box in which there were wooden rifles. We just have nothing about the distribution of the rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, when you were in the basement and Stela was giving you instructions, were the other detainees with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: In the basement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, I understand the questions that Judge Clark just had, but I believe I object to that question. It assumes facts not in evidence. The witness already testified it wasn't the individual named Stela who gave instructions in the basement; it was a different individual. So I object to the form of the question, and I also object that it's leading. I understand that any objections to asked and answered would be improper. But the leanings of the question - it assumes facts not in evidence - I object to those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Bos, would you please make it clear for us and rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: By the way, what's the specific date of that incident? You may also ask the witness to clear it up for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I can ask again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall what the date was when all this happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I think it was on the 19th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Are you a hundred percent sure about this date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, once again, we are faced with a problem of leading the witness. We had the similar problem with the name of this individual. We have a problem involving a date with this witness. And now, for the second time, the witness has given his answer. And I'm sure that the issue was a matter of preparations. I don't know. I don't see the reason for this question "Are you a hundred percent sure about this date?" I am objecting to the leading nature of this question to an issue in respect of which the witness has already given his answer twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: The witness said "I think." That's why I'm asking, "Are you a hundred percent sure?" Otherwise, he would have said, "It was on..." And then I would not have asked this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the witness has answered the question, and you may skip that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, let's go back again. When you were in the basement and you were in front of the desk with Stela behind the desk, were the other prisoners in the basement as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, not in this particular area. This was a basement for some sort of office. No one else was there. Just Stela. Stela was inside, and Dolma was standing at the door. I remember that individual. People called him "Dolma." He gave me instructions as to what I should do. I was first given a uniform. I put on the uniform and went out. Dado gave me a backpack full of stones to put it on my back, and he tied it like this on my chest, and then Mr. Stela approached --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, again, I'm going to stop you because, again, we have to do it step by step. So you were given the uniform. Were you then still in the basement when you were given the uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And after you were given the uniform, you were given a backpack. Were you still in the basement when you were given this backpack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I was only given this uniform in the basement and put it on in the basement, and the backpack was given to me in front of the basement, in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So when you were at the yard, who was there with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: These guys who were with me, I mean the prisoners, and another 30 or so members of the Convicts Battalion who were milling around. And Dado gave me this backpack full of stones on my back. He tied it like this. And then Stela came to me and put a plastic flask in my pocket, and he said, "Let the balijas think it's a Motorola." Then they called a young man by his name. I don't remember who he was. But he eventually brought us those wooden rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: When you say then "they" called this man, who called this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I cannot tell you their names -- I mean the name. I don't remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Okay. So then this man, he comes with the wooden rifles, and who gave you the wooden rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I don't recall the name of the individual who gave me the rifle. I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: But this again happened in the yard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Yes. It was all happening in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So you're there in the yard with your uniform, your rucksack, and your rifle. And then what happened after that? Did they -- what did they ask you to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: First of all, Dado took us to a passageway between the Health Centre and this other building. I don't know which one was which. I know this was the location of the Health Centre. There was a two-way street there and then another road. He said that we should cross over the street to reach this building on the other side of the street and wait for the soldiers to cross over, so if anyone should get killed or wounded, so that we could pull them out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Witness, now I'm going to refer to the sketch which was put on the overhead projector, and I'm going to ask you, first of all, to clarify the various locations which are on the sketch. Could you please look at the sketch and -- first of all, what represents number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: The building number 2 is the Health Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What represents number 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: The yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, you have testified that you were in the yard and that -- so from -- if you could indicate on the sketch from where of the yard were you taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: To this area here. There are two news-stands on the sidewalk here. First we crossed this street.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: All right. Let me first ask you, before you continue, what represents number 5?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Number 5 depicts the two news-stands which were on the pavement near the street where we came out. So we passed those two news-stands as we were crossing the street, and then we reached this road. And then somebody spoke behind us. And judging by the way he spoke, I think it was Dado. And he told us to go to the left, to the building on the left side, which is what we did. We reached a building. I don't recall exactly what the situation was because I was really overwhelmed, but I realised that I had crossed the street and ended up in a building. There was rubble falling down --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, again, sorry, I'm going to interrupt you. So you go down the street and somebody behind you - you think it's Dado - gave you instructions to go to a building on the left. Is that building which he instructed you to go, is that also depicted on this sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: It's not marked exactly. It's just the area where it could have been. This is really an approximation, my diagram. I just marked the location where I think the building was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you've also indicated something which is marked as number 1. What does number 1 -- what is that on the sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: There is a junction behind the Health Centre and a location from which the tank opened fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Right. So number 1 is the tank? Is that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said, a tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, while you were working -- walking on this road, was the tank shooting, firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And in which direction was the tank firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: The tank was stationed here, and it was firing in this direction here where these buildings are. It was probably firing at these buildings, because at the moment I reached this building, I fell down because of a detonation, and this is the location where I was wounded, probably from a shell -- from the shell which had impacted the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You said you were wounded. Where were you wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: In my leg. I can show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, you don't have to show us, Witness. No, that's all right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: On three locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: He wants to show it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You can show it, but I'm just worried about the fact that he's a protected witness and that he cannot move around. You can show the wound, but I hope that we can do that without --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Perhaps if you explain your reasons for the hesitation, it would put the witness at his ease.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, yes, my hesitation of you showing the wound was that you are being protected by facial distortion, and if you're now going to move from your desk, the public may see you. So maybe we can go into closed session and then the witness can show the wound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: It will make this witness feel happier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We do not have any problem with this. I mean, we do not contest this in any way. So as far as the Defence is concerned, we believe the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, anyway, we are going to see the wounds from this witness. We'll go to the closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, if you could just wait until we close down the blinds, and then you can stand up and show the wounds. If you just wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So Witness PP, so you got injured. Do you know what injured you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I don't know. I suppose it was a shell, but I'm not sure. Because I don't know what it was. When I came round, when I regained consciousness, I was covered with rocks, rubble, plaster. I only remember that I was pulled inside the building. I was frozen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So you actually lost conscious when you got injured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I don't remember if it was unconsciousness, but I was disoriented. My mind was not working properly. It was blocked. I remember I was inside the building, and I thought I had escaped alone, whereas there were actually three other people with me, three other men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And who were these three other men, without giving their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: The men who escaped with me. They were prisoners as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You said that you remember that you were pulled in. Who pulled you in the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, I don't remember being pulled inside. I was told that later. I don't remember that happening. I thought at the moment that I had entered the building myself, on my own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Bos, I hate to interrupt you. But as for the sketches made by this witness himself, we would like to see a real picture or real photo or map to let this sketch correspond to the real map.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can understand that. And I will try. But I hope that the witness will be able to recognise the photograph. If the witness then could be shown Exhibit 14.5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Bos, does this witness have any problem with his eyesight, seeing that he was taken out of hospital following operations to his eyes?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, you heard the question of the Judge. You were operated on your eyesight. How is your eyesight at the moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I have a problem with my left eye sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: There is now a photograph in front of -- are you able to see what's on the photograph? Witness, do you recognise what's on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: This is a totally different picture to what I remember from the day when I made my escape. For instance, what is missing on this picture are the two kiosks, the two news-stands. I'm not quite sure that this is it, because this picture looks totally different to me from what I saw when I escaped. And I wouldn't like to say anything final based on this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, considering that this photograph was taken a long time after the incident, would you still be able to recognise some of the buildings on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I can't say. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Because this looks totally different to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, let me give it one more try. Witness, you said that there were two kiosks, and you don't see these kiosks on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Would you know where these kiosks used to be? Could you indicate that on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Roughly here. That's where they should be, as far as I can say. But the picture is totally different to me from what I saw on that day. I don't know Mostar very well, and what I saw doesn't look like what's here in the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So if I would ask you which building you actually ended up on that day, would you be able to tell that from the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I wouldn't want to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, if you look at the photograph, would you know where the tank was situated on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Here, approximately, because it was at the intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And, Witness, could you indicate the yard from where you actually left with the other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, point of order. While this witness is doing these things, could he at least mark on these -- instead of just point? I know it's not my witness or anything, but for the record it might be nice to have markings, 1, 2, 3, A, B, C, whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the question is whether the witness recognised this photo or not. Well, Mr. Bos, you may try that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honours, I'm a bit reluctant to do this because the witness is clearly not very comfortable, and I really don't want him to start marking things on the photographs of which he's not 100 per cent certain of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Bos, the photograph is, after all, an aerial view, and you can remember the conditions under which this witness was operating that day, so he clearly is uncomfortable with pointing out anything on the building -- on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Are there any photographs that are not actually aerial views?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I can give it a try with a photograph which is not an aerial view, Your Honour. Your Honours, may I suggest that we break a little early for lunch and we try to find some other photographs which may help this witness to recognise certain things?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I have to warn you that during the break, you are still under the oath, so you should not talk to anybody about your testimony and do not let anybody talk to you concerning your testimony. We will continue in the afternoon with your testimony. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to have one minute of the Chamber's time after the witness is excused, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes. The usher may show you out of the room first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, thank you very much. I think I can handle this most efficiently and most quickly if we could just go into private session for one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I went through the exhibit binder, and I will ask if the witness could look at -- well, let's first let the witness look at Exhibit 14.12 first. And maybe he can also be given 14.11, just the two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I would first like you to look at Exhibit 14.12. Do you recognise what's on the photograph? My specific question on this photograph is: Would you be able to indicate on this photograph the route you took when you were actually leaving the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, because the entrance, or rather, the exit where we were was covered with sandbags, and I have a completely different idea of it. The picture seems to be different now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: All right. Can you, then, have a look at photograph 14.11, Exhibit 14.11? Now, this is a series of photographs which we pasted together, and for this photograph, can I -- can you indicate on this photograph where the tank was situated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Approximately only here, at the junction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And maybe we can put the photograph on the overhead projector and then you can -- so that's -- now, I'm afraid we will not be able to get the whole photograph on the overhead but maybe just the spot which is relevant for this particular question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: This should be the area in question here, at the junction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you get a marker and mark with a "1" where you just indicated that the tank was situated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Here, more or less. It should have been here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And looking at this photograph again, could you tell us where were you and your fellow prisoners were in relation to the tank when you were crossing this road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I'm not completely sure. I already told you that I don't know Mostar very well. This is not the image that I had in mind at the time I fled, but anyway, this should be more or less the area, the route that I took as I was trying to escape, more or less, at least the way I remember the situation, but this photograph is entirely new to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: If you say this -- could you indicate it on the map, the route you took? If you do, just take the marker and try to mark the route.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Yes. But again it will only be an approximation because I'm not sure that this is the area in question anyway. The exit that I took to get out was completely covered with sandbags and some rubble, and the situation was totally different than the one depicted on this photograph. But it was from here, more or less, that I crossed over there, and then from here I was told to go to the left to the building, more or less. But again I'm not sure, because the way I remember it, it was -- it was completely different at the time I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: All right. Well, if --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Again, Your Honours, I'm a bit hesitant to let this witness mark if he's not absolutely sure, so I would prefer he's not marking this route if he's not 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So, Witness, we will leave it with this. Witness, could you now look at Exhibit 14.9. Sorry, 14.8. 14.8. I'm sorry, it's 14.9 and 14.10. I'm sorry about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: If the witness could first be shown Exhibit 14.10.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise what's depicted on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I just don't want to venture either way, because I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I think I'm going to leave it with this, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Witness, just one -- a few questions to end this examination. When you actually -- when you actually entered the building after you had had -- after you had crossed the road, did you still have your wooden rifle on you? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I took the rifle inside the building, and it remained there, together with the backpack with the stones I was taking to one of the buildings. But I was wounded, so I had left all of my equipment there. It remained there. I no longer had an opportunity to see it because I eventually left the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So did you ever get it back? Did you get the rucksack and the wooden rifle back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you know with whom you left it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Things remained inside the building with several soldiers who were there with rifles, but I don't know what eventually happened to all those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Par, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, my name is Zelimir Par. I am an attorney at law representing Vinko Martinovic in this case, and I should like to ask you several questions concerning your testimony today. At the beginning, I should like to move into private session for the purposes of mentioning a few names of individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please. And Mr. Par, I have to warn you, you have to turn off your mike after your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, your request for the protective measures is granted by this Trial Chamber. Maybe you are not very much familiar with the equipment in this courtroom. You see the mike of Defence counsel, there is a light. When the light is on, do not answer the question. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, let us follow up on the incident involving wooden rifles which you discussed with the Prosecutor. So you do not know where your wooden rifle ended. Am I correct in understanding your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: At the moment I got inside the building and went into the cellar of that building, I left my backpack and my rifle there, and I was transferred to the other building where the infirmary was where I was given help and where I stayed that night. On the following day, I went over to the other side, and that's all I know. I cannot tell you about the things that I'm not sure about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Of course. The reason I'm asking you this question is because one of the witnesses in this case, Witness OO, and who is one of the men who was with you during this particular event, told us that he knows that all of those four rifles were taken by a member of the army. Have you heard any such thing? Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I will tell you how it was and what happened, as far as I'm concerned. I don't know what others told you. I got in. I sat down on one of the steps. I took off my backpack, and the rifle remained on the steps, and I was transferred to another basement at that point. That's all I can be sure about. I cannot claim anything that I'm not certain about, because others at that point in time were no longer with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Have you heard of a museum in which one of those rifles would have been exhibited as a kind of memento or as a souvenir from those days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen that, and I don't want to state anything about it. I haven't heard about it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: On the day that you escaped, that is, after that day, did you ever see any of these detainees who were with you in that group? Did you see them on that day and the day that followed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: As I told you, that night I was transferred to the other basement. I'm not sure. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Let us focus on that particular day. Not the next day, but that day. Did you see any one of them on that very day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, I did not because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I think we need a redaction in the transcript, and maybe the witness should be warned not to mention any names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the names will be redacted. Witness, you have to know that you should be very careful about the mentioning of the names because some of those names are under the protective measures. If you want to mention some names, just ask for the permission. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, but you should have warned me earlier on. It's not my fault. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Par, we have a difference between the English translation and the -- the English interpretation and the French interpretation. And also, we need to have pauses between questions and answers so that the interpreters can catch up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. I will bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Before you start, can we just say to the witness, who looks a little confused about the names. Witness PP, the names of the protected witnesses are the names of the people who were with you when you escaped to the other side. You can talk about anybody else, but those people have asked -- the survivors have asked for protective measures, and therefore we don't mention their names. But if either we or any of the lawyers ask you for their names, they will ask to go into private session. Now, these are words you don't normally hear of, but they are the only names we are concerned about. But what we are really concerned about is that you speak very fast. Mr. Par is every bit as fast as you are, and the translators are already having problems when you talk across each other. So just -- what the president usually explains much better than I do, so I let him, about the little dot, he's better at explaining that to witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, let me go back to my last question. My last question was whether on that day - not the following day but on that day - you saw any of the prisoners who had been with you in that group. And to be even more specific, did you see any of those prisoners carry that wooden rifle during that day or later that day? Did you see that or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I told you I didn't see because I was immediately transferred to another basement, to the infirmary, where I was given medical help, and that is the reason why I didn't see any one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us focus on the rifles. Did they have any straps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did all of them have straps, and could you describe that strap? Was it an improvised strap?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: It was an original strap from an automatic rifle. It was light green in colour, in braided form, but it was, at any rate, an original strap from an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What was the colour of the rifles and what was the shape of those rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: It was as a regular Kalashnikov rifle, painted -- painted black, with this strap from an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know who manufactured those rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether anyone else from your group had participated in the making of those rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: You're referring to those three men who were with me? No, I don't think that they had taken part in that. They were there. I don't think they had time to -- they were with me the whole time. They didn't have time to make those rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: A witness in this case, Allan Knudsen, who was a foreign mercenary, testified before this Court that he had seen the same prisoners making those rifles, the same prisoners who carried them the following day. After his testimony, a dilemma arose before all of us here because we no longer knew whether we were talking about one single incident or several such incidents. So my question to you is: Do you know this person by the name of Knudsen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No. This is the first time I hear this name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I have asked you about Mostar in general. Now I am asking you about Stela's unit specifically. Did you ever hear or see these wooden rifles being used in any other occasion except for this one in which you personally participated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: One of the prisoners who was with you in this group, and who testified as Witness OO, told us that after he had escaped, he gave a statement on that day or on that night to a military man concerning the events that had happened to him. Did the same thing happen to you? Did you give a statement with him or on your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: As I told you, I was transferred to the infirmary, I was given medical help, and I could not go over across the old bridge on that same night. So they took me to the SDK building late at night, and a doctor came to the SDK building. He examined my wound, cleaned it, and treated it. So I did talk to someone. I don't know exactly who that person was. Whether he was a policeman or a soldier, I don't know. But he was wearing a uniform. I told him about the circumstances of my capture, my arrest, where I was arrested, where I was detained, and so on and so forth, but I cannot tell you anything about the identity of this individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: As far as this interview is concerned, the interview with this official, whether he was a member of the military or the police, that is not important, but was the purpose of that interview to check on the circumstances of your being there, of your arrival to the other side, or was the purpose of that statement, of that interview, a different one? Was it an interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: The individual who conducted the interview, was it suspicious of something? Was it because he suspected you of having escaped from the other side? Was it necessary for him to check the circumstances of your escape, or was the purpose of this interrogation different?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Well, he asked me how I ended up in the camp. I didn't notice any suspicion of any sort. I was simply asked to provide them with a brief description of my capture and how I ended up on the other side. But we didn't discuss the details. I didn't spend much time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: At some later stage, after this interview, were you at any point in time called back to give a statement for the purposes of clarifying that situation? And I'm not referring to the interview with the OTP here from this Tribunal. I'm referring to the relevant authorities and the initial statement that you gave to them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I remember that an individual came on one occasion to ask me whether I was prepared to talk about what had happened to me in Mostar with the investigators of the Tribunal. That was the only such contact. And after that, I contacted the investigators of the Tribunal and gave them my statement. But other than that, no, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness, what AID is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: From the media. I heard from the media that it's some sort of police. I don't know. I have no clue, because -- but there is a lot of talk about it lately, and I heard in the media that it's some sort of secret police. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were you contacted perhaps by this secret police, AID, regarding these events, regarding your testimony? Did you have any contacts with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And this other man who had talked to you previously, whether you were prepared to testify before this Tribunal, did he introduce himself which police he was representing, whether he was from AID or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: He didn't say he was from the AID. He just appeared as an official inviting me to the police station to confirm that my statement was correct. No AID was mentioned. All I have told you is based on what I heard from the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I would very much like to ask one question. But for the sake of caution, we should better go into private session perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us, on that day when all this was going on with those wooden rifles as you have described today, how many other prisoners were able to see that event while this was going on, your escape, your movement with those wooden rifles? How many other prisoners were around who could see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I can't tell you precisely, but perhaps there were ten men around. Not many of us were standing in the yard of the Health Centre, perhaps about ten. I can't give you a precise figure. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you tell me, in your community, in your environment, was this event later discussed? Did the story make the rounds? Was it described and redescribed as part of the stories about that and similar incidents? Is it your experience that this story was making the rounds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: How shall I answer this question, I wonder? Were there stories circulating? Of course, they were. All this, the persecution, the humiliation, all this is still talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I didn't mean that; I meant this particular event involving wooden rifles. Was it discussed in the community in which you live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Lots of stories made the rounds in the place where it happened, but I left that area very soon after the event, and I went back to live in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I didn't want you to mention any places. But anyway, the notion is too broad to threaten anyone's identity. Anyway, let us focus now on this unit. Let us call it "Stela's unit," conditionally speaking. Do you know the name of that unit today, or did you know it then, this Stela's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I knew it by the name of "Convicts Battalion" or "Stelici." That's what they call themselves, the "Convicts Battalion" and "Stelici," and that's what it was in my mind. From their own words, that's all I know. If I weren't sure of that, I wouldn't be saying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood you correctly when you testified. How many times were you in that unit or with that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I can't say that precisely either. You never know where you are. You're always brought somewhere. People around tell you, "We're Stelici," or we're something else. A soldier passing by says, "We are Stelici." Those are the things I remember. I can't say precisely how many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I understand that you don't have a clear recollection precisely because of the fact that you never knew where you were exactly, and that's what creates the confusion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Yes, that's why I can't say precisely. I wasn't sure where I was. But I remember occasions where we were brought by this Vinko, Dinko Martinovic, this driver, to Stela's unit. I remember the works, the filling of bags with sand, the cladding of walls with these bags, the things we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Let us go back to this Dinko or Vinko Martinovic, which through your testimony you seem to have considered as Stela's soldier. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: During your testimony today, you seem to have said that there were occasions when Vinko was driving you on a truck and would leave two or three people behind in certain places and drive the rest of you on. Were there such occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So this driver, whatever his name, left some of the people with different units; he didn't drive all of you together to this unit called Stela's unit for practical purposes. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: You see, there were certain people like masons, like carpenters, people who had specific trades. That's how they were grouped, and that's the reason why they were left in certain places on certain work sites, because masons were needed or carpenters were needed. They were left in certain locations to work in their trade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: We are now dealing with the issue of where this zone of responsibility was which was Stela's. And which was his zone of responsibility? Can you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I cannot tell you precisely where his zone of responsibility was. I know that the Convicts Battalion was an intervention unit, and they were always located in the place where the separation line was shifting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you think that Stela is the commander of the Convicts Battalion? Do you think that was the name of his unit? Whenever you hear "Convicts Battalion," do you always associate it with Stela? Can we distinguish between these two things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I know there was one Convicts Battalion. There -- maybe there were more than one, but I know only about one Convicts Battalion, and I'm telling you only about things that I know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned during your testimony that there existed a unit named after a dog, Mrmak or something. Is that the name, another name, for the Convicts Battalion, or was it the name of another unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: That's the name of the Convicts Battalion. It was the name of Stela's dog. All of this is something I know from hearsay, from stories of others. I heard that his dog was named Mrmak, and that was the reason why a dog was depicted on their emblem, and that they were the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Sir, I understand all that. The point of my question is not whether his dog's name was Mrmak or not, but you know, you witnessed this war. There were -- there are larger and smaller units. One of these units was called Mrmak. Do you believe that Stela was the commander of this Convicts Battalion, that this was a unit of that size? When you say "Convicts Battalion" and "Stela's unit," are these synonyms in your mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. You speak too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: While testifying today, you used the term Convicts Battalion. When you said that, did you mean that members of the Convicts Battalion were soldiers under Stela's command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I think so, because they said so, that Stela was their boss, their commander. It is from this that I conclude that he was what he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now show this witness one document in order to pursue this subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, I have here a document I would like to show you. It is Prosecutor's Exhibit P626, from the twelfth binder. I will not bother you too much with this document. I would just like you to look at one sentence so we can discuss it. I will tell you what this document is. It is a brief or information drafted by SIS, which is this Croatian police, dated 7th October, 1993, and when you see this document, will you kindly look at it, see what it is about, and then concentrate on the first paragraph? Please take your time to look through the document, and if you like, you may read it in its entirety. We are only interested in the first paragraph, so you don't have to waste too much time on the rest of the document. If you have looked at it, then I can ask my question, and then, if you like, you may come back to the text before you answer. What I -- my intention was to concentrate on the first sentence, which I will read slowly. It says: "The source" -- or perhaps I will read the whole excerpt: "The source came to know that in the night of the 2nd October, 1993, the looting and expulsion of Muslim citizens from the right to the left bank continued. It has come to the source's knowledge that this is being done by groups which use the names of various units. This is confirmed by statements of the neighbours; namely, the members of these units call out to each other, conspicuously, names like Tutici, Stelici, and other names, in order to shift the blame to the wrong entity." This is the substance of the text. What I would like to know is the following: We have just been discussing something in order to establish who was who and who belonged to which unit, and you told me on what basis you believe some people to have been members of Stela's unit. Now, having read this, do you allow for the possibility that even in the events in which you were involved, certain people misrepresented themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to say anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Okay. We can set this document aside, but we cannot give up trying to establish who belonged to which unit. You say that you identify the Convicts Battalion with Stela and his unit. That's the way it seemed to you at the time. Now, the area which was his -- that zone of responsibility, do you also identify it with Stela, that is, Vinko Martinovic? When you hear "Convicts Battalion," do you immediately think "That's where Stela was"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I have a specific question now. One incident which happened on Santiceva Street was mentioned during your testimony. One of the soldiers killed someone with a hand grenade. In your mind, is this in any way related to Stela and his unit? Do you think it was their zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: A fellow came, drunken, to the place when we were digging a trench at the entrance to the building --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Sir, please, we are clear about the event. We are reluctant to raise it again in the first place. But I'm just asking you, who was this soldier? Do you believe that this place where the incident happened was under the control of Vinko Martinovic, Stela, and his unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I will quote the words of one of the soldiers who was there -- sorry, one of the prisoners. He said, "If Stelici continuing dropping in on us like this every day, there will be no more balijas left to carry out the works."

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I will show you another document, and we'll continue this discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a document here that we've seen before. It's Exhibit P496 from Binder 10. It's a report from the administration of military police related to the 5th July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Please look at this report, and I would like to ask you a couple of questions about it. I would like to draw your attention to what is written on the first page, "the Health Centre," and then on the second page, "Aleksica Kuca, or Aleksica houses near the underpass." If I may lead you, and I should like you to confirm what I say. "Report of the police, 4th, 5th July, 1993." First line: "The bank, the old grammar school." And underneath: "Nine military policemen, reserve positions held by" -- "nine military policemen holding the position with 44 additional policemen on alert. The reserve position is held by MUP with 12 men, and 24 on alert." Second paragraph, line: "The old grammar school, Health Centre. The 9th battalion, 3rd Brigade of the HVO. The line is manned by 25 soldiers, 13 at the elementary school, 12 at the Sipad company." Third paragraph: The Health Centre again. "The position is manned by the ATG Mrmak. Due to frequent provocations ..." and so on and so forth. "The number of people manning this position is not stated in this case." Let us turn the page and see the following paragraph, the line: "At the Aleksica houses. The position is manned by the ATG Benko Penavic." The paragraph underneath, the line: "At Aleksica houses and underpass. The position is manned by the 4th Battalion of the 3rd Brigade." I don't need to go any further. But we can see that this is one of the daily reports which were regularly submitted and shows - at least as far as I'm concerned - that there were several units along the same axis. Would you agree with that? Would you agree with the fact that at the time you were there, there were several various units at those positions in addition to the ATG Mrmak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: You're referring to the dates in question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I'm referring to the confrontation line at the time you were there. I'm not trying to link it to any particular date.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, I really don't know. I'm reluctant to give any such comment because, for example, as far as this date is concerned, the 4th or the 5th of July, I was in Dretelj. But at any rate, I am really not sure about the situation on those positions and the units involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So, Witness, I'm not saying that you were there on this particular date, but my case is that the situation remained unchanged. When you were at the location, when you went to work at Stela's unit, did you happen to see there were various units there, or was it your understanding that all of the troops were members of Stelici, or the Stela's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: At least that's what they called themselves. I did not have any access to them. I did not have an opportunity to talk to any of them. But those were their own words.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Well, we already had an opportunity to see that they sometimes misrepresented the situation, but I do not intend to pursue the matter any further. If I'm correct, you were sent to work at various locations, Rodoc, Bijelo Polje, and others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I went to the area of Bijelo Polje, Rastani, Sovici, Doljani, and at other locations in the area of Mostar, and around the town of Mostar, but I cannot be more specific because I am not familiar with the town of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you what the distance was from Rodoc to Bijelo Polje in kilometres. How far were those locations? How long did it take you to get there by truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I did not mention Bijelo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I apologise, let me try this way. What was the distance between those locations? How long was the stretch to the locations where you were taken to, to perform work? I'm -- you don't have to be precise. Is it several kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Yes, several kilometres. Sovici is just several kilometres away. Rastani is not very far from the Heliodrom. Buna is also not very far from the Heliodrom. The longest distance was Sovici Doljani, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It was my fault, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have to pause. The interpreters really have some difficult time with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well, I don't wish to complicate the matter any further. I just wanted to ask you whether the -- whether members of the Stela's unit were at all those locations. But if you're not sure, you don't have to answer my question. Let us now go back to the issue which Mr. Bos tried to clarify by using a map. Witness PP, you couldn't find your way around on this map and the photograph. You said that the situation has changed in the meantime. I should like to know when was the last time that you visited the spot where you escaped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: The last time I was there was sometime in 1998 or 1999, when I went there with a friend of mine, and I showed him the area. I wanted to retrace my steps, and I remembered that there were 95 steps between two points. The distance was 95 steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, so you did visit the spot some two or three years ago. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Yes, I visited that spot. I think he told me that I must have got out from the Health Centre, at the time I was trying to escape, and he was trying to explain to me what happened and where I was, but I wasn't sure because, once again, I had a completely different picture in my mind, because I don't think I will be able to see it in the same way that it appeared to me at that moment. You can show me any picture, any photograph, you want. Again, I don't think I'll be able to tell you with certainty that that indeed was the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Sir, I fully understand you. The situation has changed indeed. But we had an opportunity to see a contemporary photograph today, and I just wanted to ask you whether the location at the time you visited it looked the same way as it looked on the photograph. Were the buildings the same?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, no, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So are you saying that at the time you visited the location, it was different from the photograph that you had -- that you saw today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Yes. This is all completely new to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And who was that friend of yours? You don't need to mention his name. Was he an official of some sort? How was it that he knew about those events? Was he an eyewitness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, he was not an eyewitness, but he happened to be -- at the moment of my escape, he was in one of those buildings. Of course, he was there. He's a friend of mine. I know him. I've known him since childhood. But he was not an official of any sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So you were not able to identify the Health Centre on that occasion either? I simply wanted to establish whether it was possible for us to see the photograph once again and ask several questions regarding the Health Centre once again, in view of that visit of yours of the location. But just tell me: Do you think there is any point in seeing the photograph once again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, I don't think there is. I really cannot be sure. I cannot tell you about things that I'm not sure about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Let us try to clear up the issue of date, if we can. Now, we are talking about the relevant event on the day when you escaped. Could you tell us what date it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I think -- at least the date that I have in my mind is the 19th of September. That's the mind -- that's the date that I have in my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: We will go back to that. Let us try to establish that we are talking about the same event. At what time did the attack start, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: At noon, thereabouts. I cannot be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How long did the attack last approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Once again, I'm not sure. I cannot be precise. I was beside myself at that moment. I don't know how long it lasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, we fully understand your situation. I am not asking you to tell us how many minutes or how many hours it lasted. However, could you give us at least a rough estimation, a rough estimate, as to how long it was? Did it last the whole day, for example? Throughout the afternoon? Or --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, not the whole day. I mean, maybe 15 or 20 minutes, from the time I got out of the building up until the moment I escaped. What happened afterwards, I don't know, because I was in this other building, in the infirmary, so I don't know how it ended or how long it actually lasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So on that day, on the day of your escape, there was a tank there which opened fire at one point. Did you hear at some later stage that the tank was there on another day, or is it the only day and the only incident that you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I remember that particular day, and I remember that it was firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I'm not trying to dispute that; I'm trying to establish the specific date because there may have been other similar events before that day or perhaps later.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I can only speak about that particular day and about what happened to me. I cannot tell you anything specific about other days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Let us dwell on the event itself for a while. Is it the same event involving the three individuals whose name we cannot mention? You were in that situation only on that particular day with those three individuals at the time, on the day when you escaped? And is it the incident involving the wooden rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I have already stated my position, and I abide by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: The reason for all these questions is because I believe that there are certain problems regarding the date. Why? Because other individuals, the men who were with you, had a different date in mind. They specifically spoke about the 17th of September, 1993. We have a document here which also mentions the same date, that is, the 17th of September, 1993, and the same event. Do you remember where you were on the 17th of September, 1993? Do you remember that particular day -- or rather, that particular date? Do you know where you were on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So why is it that you say that the event took place on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: That is the date that has remained imprinted in my mind, although I have already told you that I'm not hundred percent sure of the date. However, I remember the event as having taken place on the 19th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And this brings me finally to the following question: Do you allow for the possibility of a mistake? Is it possible that you have made a mistake regarding the date? Do you think it is possible that the event took place on the 17th of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I never offered my guarantees that the event happened on the 19th. I told you that I was not hundred percent sure. I said that I remember it as the 19th, thereabouts. But once again, I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I understand your position. And I accept your answer. But you have to understand also our position. We are trying to clarify the matter not only because of you but because of the case in general and because we want to make certain comparisons and clarify the dilemma that exists concerning this particular event. So we are now clear that we are talking about one and single event involving you and three other individuals. It may have happened on some other date, but that was the -- that is the event that we are talking about. We had a witness in this case who spoke about the time when the event started. He mentioned the event as involving some wooden rifles, but he said that the attack had started at 5.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: That is not correct. I left the Heliodrom at around 6.00. But I am sure that the event took place around noon. It may have been at 1.00 p.m., but I'm sure that it was at that time, that part of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: We are now discussing the event itself. And your group, the group of people who escaped. How was it that you made that decision? Is it something that you had previously discussed? Was it a spontaneous thing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: There was no decision whatsoever. We trusted our instincts. I didn't give the whole idea very much thought. There were no preparations whatsoever for the escape. I simply did it. I would be lying to you if I told you a different story. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you see or hear about any cases of some prisoners volunteered -- who volunteered to recover the bodies of killed soldiers or the bodies of the wounded so as to be released in return and given an opportunity to go to third countries? Have you heard of such a case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No, no, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: At the moment you were running across the separation line trying to escape, was there any shooting from infantry weapons, or just from this artillery piece that was there? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: The fire was coming from all sides. All kinds of weapons were involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, did you happen to see Stela then and there at the separation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I did not see him at the line, but I have seen him in the basement. I have already told you that I did not see him at the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Do you know a soldier by the name of Takac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Not personally, but I've heard about him. But I do not wish to give any comments on that because I'm really not sure. I don't want to recount other people's stories.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you see Takac at the separation line that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I told you, I cannot comment anything about Takac. I've heard stories about him, but I don't know who the man is, so I cannot speak about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Good. Let us focus our attention to the hospital, that is, to the time of your transfer to Mostar and the time that you spent hospitalised in that hospital. You testified that members of the Convicts Battalion used to come to the hospital, they introduced themselves the way they did, and you also told us that you had seen some insignia on them. I'm interested now in the emblem, in the insignia of that unit. Correct me if I'm wrong, but I believe that you said that you had seen the insignia with the dog's head on those soldiers with the name of the dog written underneath the picture, the image, and also the words "Convicts Battalion." Am I correct in interpreting your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Something else was written as well, "Martinovic," but I can't remember. I don't wish to state anything in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: We have to clarify the issue because my client, Mr. Martinovic, claims that there had never been an insignia like that, that they only had an insignia with the words "Vinko Skrobo" written on it and that that insignia was in use sometime between end August and September 1993. Did you happen to see such an insignia? Did you ever hear about an insignia like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I remember seeing it. I cannot describe it to you in precise terms because I don't fully remember the details, but I remember a dog's head. I don't know what units were there in the month of August. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, I understand that you're not familiar with those facts, and this is probably not something that you consider to be very important; however, I'm in a position to prove what soldiers they were, so therefore we have to establish whether the soldiers in question were members of that particular unit or not. You mentioned a name of a soldier as a member of that group, Stela's unit, and you told us that his name was Dzemo Skobalj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you personally know that man from before? Did you know him well, or only by sight, or is it the first time that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: I had known him from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you at some point in time learn that Dzemo Skobalj was a member of the unit which was commanded by Vinko Martinovic, Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I will now take the liberty of showing you another document. Please have a look at it, and we'll discuss it briefly. It is Prosecutor's Exhibit P704 from binder 4. It's a document which we have seen more than once in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the usher's assistance, I would like to show it to the witness so I can ask a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters' note: If it may be put on the ELMO as well? We don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Have you got another copy for us to put on the ELMO, for us to look at?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll give my own copy to be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, the usher will now give you this red file with an excerpt marked, and please read the title. Could you please read the title aloud?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PP
utterances.text: "Department of Defence, Convicts Battalion, ATG -- ATJ."

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What the usher has just given you is the full list, and would you kindly look through it to ascertain its contents? And we'll come to the part where it says: "ATG Vinko Skrobo." So please look through it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: How is that relevant? It's six months or five months later. It's November 1993, and we are talking about July, August, September.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we will be able to show that there were no significant changes in this unit. And in any event, there are no earlier lists. And precisely at that time, the unit - and I have to state the Defence's case now - the unit was established in this particular period. What I mean to say is that this is the only information we have about the unit. We are showing that it is these people who made up the unit and that before that time, the unit did not exist, so no one could have heard about it. I thought it might be inappropriate only insofar as this is a very long period we are talking about, but I can withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Par, if I understand, you've just said that you would be in a position to prove that this unit did not exist until November 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. That unit had two names. One name was Mrmak, the other was Vinko Skrobo. We are not making an issue out of it. It was one unit. We are saying at the time when the conflict began in Mostar between Muslims and Croats on the 9th of May, the unit had not been established. It was a different activity at the time, and the unit was formed later. We're just talking about the date of its establishment, nothing else. And that's our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: But it's important to know what you're actually saying to this witness. Are you saying that there was no unit at the medical centre whose commander was your client, Mr. Stela, Vinko Martinovic? Or are you saying that in May and June of that year, that it was called "Stelici" or something else? What are you actually saying, that its name was different, or that it didn't exist?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm telling this witness the person that he mentioned as Dzemo Skobalj, whom he knew personally and whom he considered to be a member of Stela's unit at the time, I am telling this witness in no unclear terms that my client says that this person Dzemo Skobalj was not in Stela's unit, and that's why I am offering this list, to see which soldiers were in the unit. So I'm only saying that this soldier was not one of Stela's men, and he cannot conclude on the basis of seeing that man that the men who were around the hospital that day were part of Stela's unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par, I think Judge Clark asked you a very relevant question; that is, the incident in the hospital was supposed to happen on the 9th of May, and this list, I think the date is December 2nd, 1993. There is about -- at least half a year. And some people maybe deserted, some people died. How could you prove a certain person which is not on the list was not present in May of that year?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot prove that, and I'm not offering evidence to that effect. But if the question -- I really don't know the exact date of the event at the hospital. But if it is the 9th of May, 1993, in that case - I am also responding to the Honourable Judge Clark's question - then on the 9th of May, the unit which also included Vinko Martinovic had not yet been established under either name, Vinko Skrobo or Mrmak. It was established immediately after that. But on that particular date, the unit had not yet been established; it had not had a commander. It will come into being a little while later. So I appreciate your remarks. I cannot prove anything with this document at all, and I'm withdrawing it, offering at the same time my apologies for wasting your time. It is 4.00 now, and I still have a number of questions that I propose to deal with yesterday [as interpreted], if you have no other suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 21st day of November, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
